text: FINAL INSERTION TEXTS (Planner, round-52 — verified: workspace create --mesh and agent spawn --mesh/--workspace/--role Orchestrator all exist, so the prompt cites real tooling). These are PINNED VERBATIM; the worker inserts them as-is, adjusting only surrounding markdown glue. TEXT A (general_agent.md, new bullet immediately after 'Orchestrator is an explicit mode…'): '**Machine scope, not project scope.** Your remit is this machine: its environment, its agents, and coordination across projects and peers. When a request — user, mesh, or another agent — asks for sustained work on a specific project, route it into that project'\''s workspace: spawn or reuse an orchestrator there and hand off, keeping the return address. Answer quick one-off questions directly; taking over a project'\''s execution yourself needs an explicit user ask.' TEXT B (orchestrator_suffix.md, one paragraph near the toolset/reporting rules): 'Cross-machine work: to drive work on another machine, create your own presence there — a workspace on the project checkout plus an orchestrator pane, both via `--mesh PEER` — and coordinate with it peer-to-peer; reports home back to your plan. Ask the remote machine'\''s General agent only for machine-level facts (paths, health, what runs where) or as a last resort when workspace tooling fails; project work handed to a General agent gets redirected into a workspace, not executed.' DESIGN NOTES: (1) the quick-answer escape hatch in A is deliberate — without it every trivial project question would force a spawn, agents would ignore the rule, and the rule would die; (2) B states BOTH sides of the contract (what the orchestrator does, what the GA will do) so the redirect expectation is mutual; (3) wiring-test key phrases: 'Machine scope, not project scope' and 'Cross-machine work:'. Everything else in the task stands (wiring tests, evals/cli-agent GA-redirect scenario, <=4-line budget per insertion).

SCOPE ADDITION (round-53, user): TEXT C — blocked-task triage discipline, same lane (third tiny insertion, same wiring-test pattern). ROOT CAUSE it fixes: task_b68b897f sat blocked/pane-gone with no owner action, and the FINAL gate sat blocked with no recorded unblock trigger — nothing in the prompts says a blocked task demands a live next step. INSERT into orchestrator_suffix.md, appended to the existing 'Heartbeat rules' block as one more bullet, VERBATIM: '- A blocked task is a claim, not a parking spot: every blocked task must carry a live owner action — reassign it (pane-gone), open a decision gate, or route it to your Planner with what would unblock it, and record the unblock trigger on the task. Blocked-without-a-next-step is drift; sweep for it on every heartbeat.' Wiring-test key phrase: 'a claim, not a parking spot'. Budget: this is the third and LAST insertion in this lane; total prompt growth across all three stays <=12 lines.

TEXT D + CAP AMENDMENT (round-55). Amending my own 'third and LAST insertion' pin: TEXT D lands in orchestration_toolset.md (a DIFFERENT file — the suffix <=12-line budget stands untouched; mechanics belong in the toolset, not role identity). OVERLAP CHECK against existing work (user asked): the no-poll rule EXISTS but only for REPORTS (orchestrator_suffix.md line 2: 'Do NOT use sleep or poll for reports... auto-injected') — shell gates are uncovered, which is exactly the hole Puccini fell into; wake-on-report (done) fixed injected-delivery submit, irrelevant to shell panes; reflection tripwire (done) covers integration-checkout edits only. So TEXT D is NEW scope, not duplication. INSERT VERBATIM into orchestration_toolset.md: 'Long-running shell gates (builds, soaks, remote regressions): never wait by polling — sleep/get-text loops are implementer-mode waiting. Give the command a completion contract at launch: <cmd>; codeterm send --pane 636d967b [--mesh <your-peer>] "GATE:<task_id> rc=0" — then record the gate on the task and work other frontier items until the marker arrives. For an already-running command, start a companion watcher in that pane (while pgrep -f <name> >/dev/null; do sleep 30; done; codeterm send ...): the wait runs remotely, never in your loop.' Wiring-test key phrase: 'completion contract at launch'.

PIN CORRECTION (round-56, supersedes TEXT D placement): Planner survey found orchestration_toolset.md is a DEAD FILE — no include_str loader exists; all its edits this effort never shipped. TEXT D text stands VERBATIM but its placement is now owned jointly with the new dead-prompt-files task: land TEXT D wherever the toolset content lives after that fix (newly wired file, or orchestrator_onboard.rs inline block). Do not insert into a file that does not load.

TEXT E (round-80, Andrey: 'если чего-то не понимает — обращается к планировщику; хочу чтоб так было внутри планнинг-механизма'). INSERT into orchestrator_suffix.md, appended to the Planning-ownership block, VERBATIM: 'When something is unclear — a task'\''s intent, a finding'\''s meaning, how to sequence, whether a report satisfies the criteria — ask your Planner before guessing or stalling: send the specific question with what you already tried. Uncertainty routed early is planning working; uncertainty ground through alone becomes a bounce.' Wiring-test key phrase: 'ask your Planner before guessing'. Symmetric line for planner_suffix.md (one sentence): 'Answer orchestrator questions with decisions and rationale, not options — you are the tie-breaker, and an unanswered question stalls the frontier.' Wiring key: 'decisions and rationale, not options'. Budget note: TEXT A-E total across both suffixes stays within the charter's stranger's-repo + brevity constraints; E is the LAST insertion this lane accepts — further prompt asks go to the audit task's follow-ups.
